answer: A haven admits a newcomer only when two identities drawn by lot from the atlas, disjoint from its own cluster, each stake their whole nectar against its conduct. Nectar accrues only through settled trade with parties outside the holder's cluster, so it cannot be self-minted, and any pair that signs is struck from the pool forever. The kth identity under one hand needs k further unrelated pairs, each forfeiting nectar that never returns, so a thousand clones burn a thousand outsiders' accrued stake and each bribe climbs as the pool thins. An honest newcomer pays the same first pair.
